title: How much harder a second ethics finding lands than the first
usableAnswer: Per researched body (or as a national pattern where bodies do not publish schedules): how penalties change for a repeat violator, whether referral or disqualification follows, and any evidence on the electoral cost of a second finding relative to a first.
whyItMatters: The owner asked on 2026-09-22 that getting caught more than once cost more. The game now charges payments made after a finding in a second round and raises the second fine and vote loss by a placeholder, so every repeat offender in every state escalates by the same invented step.

answer.summary: Senate 2025 records 181 new allegations, 5 carried matters and 27 preliminary inquiries; overlapping stages cannot establish a personal-use cohort disposition rate. FEC guidance describes confidential complaint review and possible civil conciliation, without a universal time or repeat-sanction multiplier. No defensible universal vote penalty follows from these counts.
